result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_edge_attrs()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get edge attribute values. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L7310-L7393){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_edge_attrs( edge_attr, sources=None, targets=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Extracts a specific attribute from edges. Can optionally filter by source and/or target nodes. Returns a dictionary keyed by edge IDs. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [edge_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The name of the attribute to get. [sources]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional list of source node IDs/labels to filter edges. [targets]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional list of target node IDs/labels to filter edges. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, any]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Dictionary mapping edge IDs (integers) to attribute values. Only includes edges that have the attribute set. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#ebdd7117 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node("A") .add_node("B") .add_node("C") .add_node("D") .add_edge("A", "B", weight=1.5, type="friend") .add_edge("B", "C", weight=2.0, type="colleague") .add_edge("C", "D", weight=1.0, type="friend") ) graph.get_edge_attrs("weight") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {1: 1.5, 2: 2.0, 3: 1.0} ``` ::: ::: Any attribute name works the same way, including custom ones like `type`: ::: {#0a742e92 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.get_edge_attrs("type") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {1: 'friend', 2: 'colleague', 3: 'friend'} ``` ::: :::
